newsitem.title: UK: Reuters says to find way to return cash.
newsitem.headline: Reuters says to find way to return cash.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc hopes to find a way to return cash to shareholders despite a proposed change in the UK rules on tax credits on share buybacks, the company's chief executive Peter Job said on Wednesday.

"It is necessary for some way to be found in which cash can be given out to shareholders without excessive problems, and no doubt this will happen in due course," Job told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Earlier, shareholders in the international news and information group voted to delay consideration of plans to return cash in a share buyback and special bonus dividend issue.
On Tuesday the British government said it would abolish a system of tax credits on such schemes.
The announcement came only a day before Reuters shareholders were to due vote on proposals for the 613 million stg scheme and prompted Reuters to ask them to adjourn consideration of the plans.
Job said Reuters had taken advice from leading tax counsel on the scheme and had been told it was within the framework of the law before the changes to legislation.
The company would now reassess its position but the underlying need was for it to be able to return cash to shareholders in a tax neutral way.
"The company doesn't need the cash. It should be able to return it to shareholders in a tax-neutral way," he said.
"If we have to keep it then there's pressure to pay regular dividends or to acquire other companies which may not be our actual commercial priority," he added.
Job said he did not see the cash position as a problem.
"I don't see having cash as that much of a problem and besides we have an awful lot of investments to do going forward," he said.
